Checked OK: the locationNote's case list is right: Digital Rights Ireland was decided on 8 April 2014, Schrems I on 6 October 2015 and Schrems II on 16 July 2020, all by the Court of Justice in Luxembourg. The local file opens (960x720) and shows a row of EU flags on a lawn in front of the dark Palais and low brown buildings, as the alt text says. The thumbUrl returns HTTP 200.

Note, no change required: in November 2006 the court was formally the Court of Justice of the European Communities. The name 'Court of Justice of the European Union' dates from the Lisbon Treaty (1 December 2009). The caption follows Commons in using today's name for the buildings, which is acceptable. An editor who wants strict period accuracy could write 'buildings of what is now the Court of Justice of the European Union'.

issues: Licence OK: I re-fetched the Commons page. 'This file is licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution 2.0 Generic license.' is verbatim, and FlickreviewR 2 confirmed cc-by-2.0 on 11 May 2023. The upstream Flickr page (flickr.com/photos/72132190@N08/52886976440) loads with the title 'EKO - AI ACT - Strasbourg Parliament', username 'Ekō', pathAlias 'eko_movement', dateTaken '2023-05-10 14:15:21' and licence creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0. fetch-text --check FOUND for the full Commons description 'Ekō delivered a booklet to the 2 co-rapporteurs in charge of the file containing our open letter and Ekō members' messages regarding the inclusion of generative AI systems in the functional section of the upcoming AI Act.'

Attribution incomplete: the file's EXIF on the Commons page names the photographer as 'Author Thomas Cytrynowicz' and the 'Copyright holder' as 'Jugaad Prod - Thomas Cytrynowicz' (fetch-text --check FOUND for 'Jugaad Prod - Thomas Cytrynowicz'). Ekō is the Flickr account and licensor, not the photographer. The creator and creditLine should name the photographer. The CC BY licence granted by Ekō's account stands, as Commons accepted it.

Alt text wrong: it says the three people are 'standing at a table'. The image shows them seated around a low glass coffee table in lounge chairs. The woman sits in a grey chair, and the man in the centre is seated. The booklets carry the 'EKO' logo.

Independent: the EP briefing 'Newsletter - 8-11 May 2023 - Strasbourg plenary session' confirms that 10 May 2023 fell in a Strasbourg plenary week. The EP press release 20230505IPR84904 (datetime 2023-05-11) says 'On Thursday, the Internal Market Committee and the Civil Liberties Committee adopted a draft negotiating mandate' on the AI Act. It names the two co-rapporteurs verbatim, 'co-rapporteur Brando Benifei (S&D, Italy)' and 'Co-rapporteur Dragos Tudorache (Renew, Romania)', so the handover came the day before the committee vote. The caption's facts are right. The fix below adds the sourced names and the timing, and does not rely on identifying faces.
thumbCheck is out of date: it records HTTP 429. I re-checked the thumbUrl today and it returns HTTP 200 image/jpeg. The local file opens (960x640).

fieldFixes.caption: At the European Parliament in Strasbourg on 10 May 2023, the campaign group Ekō delivers a booklet containing its open letter and members' messages to the two co-rapporteurs in charge of the AI Act file (Brando Benifei and Dragoș Tudorache, per the Parliament). The letter concerned the inclusion of generative AI systems in the upcoming AI Act; the next day the Parliament's internal-market and civil-liberties committees adopted their AI Act negotiating mandate.
fieldFixes.alt: Three people seated around a low glass table in a busy parliament lounge, a woman handing blue Ekō booklets to two men in suits
fieldFixes.creator: Thomas Cytrynowicz (Jugaad Prod) for Ekō (formerly SumOfUs)
